purpose: Join family-specific route blocker localization to predictive intervention timing while allowing current physically derived dynamic escape timing to replace stale certified baseline timing when degraded-state evidence requires it.
invariants: Route safety owns blocker localization and route-family hazard semantics.
Predictive safety owns whether intervention can complete before the conservative blocker or commitment boundary.
Dynamic escape authority owns the current machinery response burden when degraded-state evidence is supplied.
A route blocker distance may be consumed as predictive input only when route safety marks it as applicable to the certified blocker.
Dynamic escape timing may increase the intervention burden from physically modeled degraded state but may not invent generic damage or technology multipliers.
Missing blocker geometry, progress rate, timing, power, thermal, actuation or family evidence remains UNRESOLVED rather than becoming zero.
PRECOMMIT and PORTAL_ADMISSION families do not receive fabricated continuous route velocities.
Predictive PASS does not erase a route REJECTED disposition; route ADMISSIBLE does not erase predictive or dynamic-escape BLOCK.
provenanceRequirements: Preserve the complete dynamic-escape packet when required.
Record which blocker field supplied the predictive distance.
Record whether the distance was conservative, nominal, or unavailable.
Record whether intervention time came from current dynamic escape evidence or the certified static baseline.
Record all explicit overrides separately from route-derived evidence.
